problems: interestPaidSince (accountlife.ts:170-172) matches a term's taken interest by memo alone: t.memo === `Interest: ${account.name}`. Every term at a bank has the same name, term.called (lending.ts, bank.open_term), and take_term_interest (:484) and maturity (:684) both post that memo. So canceling a new term reverses interest paid by an older term of the same product after the new one opened. It takes it back out of the primary, takes it off the year's income (recordInterest), and counts it in cancelRefusal's refusal. Probe (scratchpad/probe/term3.ts), Berlin, Deutsche Bank: term A of €10,000 opened; 10 days later term B of €10,000 opened; a day later A's €6.93 taken; B canceled. Result: 'Interest returned: FestzinsSparen, canceled' posts AktivKonto -693 and Interest +693. The primary ends €6.93 short of what it should hold, and A is still open with its interest gone. This is reachable abroad at every bank with interestDuringTerm.

The cooling-off ends at the opening moment's time of day on the last day: coolingOffEnds (accountlife.ts:272, :275) and afterBusinessDays (bankdays.ts:55-63) return openedAt shifted by whole days, and inCoolingOff tests sim.now <= ends. The panel says 'until <that date>' (BankAccountLife.tsx, formatDate(ends)), and both rules cover the whole last day: 'within 14 business days after the day on which ... opened' (SOR/2021-181 s.5(1)) and 'diez días hábiles posteriores'. Probe (scratchpad/probe/lastday.ts): Toronto, an RBC account opened 5 January at 7:30 AM; the panel says until January 23; at 11:30 AM on 23 January Cancel It is refused 'Its cooling-off period has passed'. Mexico City (Banorte) is the same: until January 19, refused at 11:30 AM on the 19th. The calendar-day countries do the same, as they did before. The Banorte test cancels at 9 AM on 10 February against a noon opening, so it never meets the boundary.
The threshold mutation the result marks 'not run' (`amount <= into.balance + 1`, accountlife.ts:251) survives: the Berlin term test tries only primary balances of 0 and exactly 6_30, never 6_29.
The guide's 'In Canada and Mexico the fees charged while it was open are refunded, but not overdraft interest' leaves out the machine owner's fee, which is also excluded (:206). This is minor.
